plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The leaves emerge the following spring and die back by early summer. All parts of the plant are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe, including the UK, France, Germany, and the Alps; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used to treat gout and used in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling. It is often called 'naked ladies' because the flowers appear without leaves.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms dense clumps topped with plume-like clusters of tiny yellow flower heads. It is an important late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other insects.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America in meadows, roadsides, and prairies; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time. Goldenrod pollen is heavy and sticky and is spread by insects, not wind.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with strappy leaves and tall, leafless stems topped by umbels of frilly, sparkling pink flowers with wavy-edged petals. It thrives in sunny, well-drained spots and flowers when most other plants are fading.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa; widely grown in gardens in the UK, Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Nerine petals have a glittering, shimmering surface that sparkles in sunlight, which is why they are sometimes called 'diamond lilies'.

plants.name: Clianthus puniceus
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with arching branches, feathery leaves, and clusters of dramatic claw-shaped, bright red flowers resembling a parrot's beak. In the Southern Hemisphere, it blooms in the spring, attracting native birds such as tūī and bellbirds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: New Zealand's North Island; now rare in the wild but common in cultivation
plants.funFact: Kākābeak is among New Zealand's most endangered native plants in the wild, largely because of browsing by introduced animals, but it is easily grown in gardens, which helps preserve it.
